'''Isaiah Miller Jr.''' (born November 9, 1997)<ref>{{cite web |title=Isaiah Miller |url=https://www.nba.com/stats/player/1630627 |website=NBA.com |access-date=10 October 2025}}</ref> is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Austin Spurs]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UNC Greensboro Spartans men's basketball|UNC Greensboro Spartans]].

==Early life==
Miller was born in [[Norfolk, Virginia]] but grew up in [[Covington, Georgia]]. He attended [[Eastside High School (Covington, Georgia)|Eastside High School]] in Covington before transferring to [[Newton High School (Georgia)|Newton High School]] before his senior year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thetimesnews.com/sports/20170512/uncg-adds-basketball-transfer-from-wichita-state|title=UNCG adds basketball transfer from Wichita State|work=[[Times-News (Burlington, North Carolina)|Times-News]]|date=May 12, 2017|access-date=March 6, 2020}}</ref> As a senior, Miller averaged 20 points, six rebounds and 3.1 steals per game in leading the team to a 28–2 record and Region 8-AAAAAA championship. He was named first team All-Region and All-County and honorable mention All-State. He committed to [[UNC Greensboro Spartans men's basketball|UNC Greensboro]] in May 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.covnews.com/sports/newton/newtons-isaiah-miller-commits-to-unc-greensboro/|title=Newton's Isaiah Miller commits to UNC-Greensboro|first=Gabriel|last=Stovall|work=[[The Covington News]]|date=May 7, 2017|access-date=March 6, 2020}}</ref>

==College career==
Miller served as a key reserve at point guard as a true freshman, playing in all 35 of the Spartans' games and was named to the [[Southern Conference]] All-Freshman team after averaging 8.3 points and 1.4 steals per game, which was 8th-best in the conference.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.greensboro.com/sports/college/jeff-mills-isaiah-miller-emerges-as-uncg-basketball-adjusts-to/article_ae91a7c5-8ef7-5865-9d62-0c0c36eaf9a5.html|title=Jeff Mills: Isaiah Miller emerges as UNCG basketball adjusts to life after Francis Alonso|first=Jeff|last=Mills|work=[[News & Record]]|access-date=March 6, 2020}}</ref> He became UNC Greensboro's starting point guard during his sophomore year and averaged 15.2 points, 4.5 rebounds, 2.1 assists and conference-best 2.9 steals per game and was named first team All-SoCon.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2019/07/23/unc-greensboro-basketball-isaiah-miller-frontrunner-southern-poy-2019-20/|title=UNC Greensboro Basketball: Isaiah Miller frontrunner for Southern POY in 2019-20|first=Tristan|last=Freeman|website=bustingbrackets.com|date=23 July 2019 |access-date=March 6, 2020}}</ref> His 104 steals were the second most in school history and in the NCAA Division I for the 2018–19 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rockdalenewtoncitizen.com/sports/former-newton-standout-isaiah-miller-making-big-impact-at-unc/article_dfc7820a-209c-11ea-baa0-5385ca5b8155.html|title=Former Newton standout Isaiah Miller making big impact at UNC Greensboro|work=[[The Rockdale Citizen]]|date=December 17, 2019|access-date=March 6, 2020}}</ref> As a junior, Miller was named first team All-SoCon, the conference Defensive Player of the Year and the [[Southern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Southern Conference Player of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rockdalenewtoncitizen.com/sports/isaiah-miller-named-socon-player-of-the-year-defensive-player/article_e61f78c4-5e81-11ea-8ca2-b3946f8e4904.html|title=Isaiah Miller named SoCon Player of the Year, Defensive Player of the Year|work=[[The Rockdale Citizen]]|date=March 4, 2020|access-date=March 6, 2020}}</ref> He averaged 17.8 points and 2.8 steals per game. Following the season, Miller entered the [[2020 NBA draft]] but did not sign with an agent.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Mills |first1=Jeff |title=UNCG's Isaiah Miller enters NBA Draft |url=https://www.greensboro.com/sports/college/uncgs-isaiah-miller-enters-nba-draft/article_51494e06-a050-5726-9eaa-1cf6ecf863dd.html |access-date=April 5, 2020 |work=[[News & Record]] |date=April 3, 2020}}</ref> On July 22, he announced he was returning for his senior season.<ref>{{cite news |title=UNCG's Isaiah Miller will return for senior basketball season |url=https://journalnow.com/sports/uncgs-isaiah-miller-will-return-for-senior-basketball-season/article_df208528-e67c-5b5d-8c08-8f5993e13d34.html |access-date=August 2, 2020 |work=[[Winston-Salem Journal]] |date=July 22, 2020}}</ref>

For the 2020–21 season, Miller repeated as the unanimous SoCon Player and Defensive Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite press release|url=https://soconsports.com/news/2021/3/3/all-southern-conference-mens-basketball-teams-announced.aspx|title=All-Southern Conference men's basketball teams announced|publisher=[[Southern Conference]] |date=March 3, 2021 |access-date=March 3, 2021}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Iowa Wolves (2021–2022)===
After going undrafted in the 2021 NBA draft, Miller joined the Minnesota Timberwolves for the 2021 NBA Summer League and on September 20, 2021, he signed with the Timberwolves.<ref>{{cite web|title=TIMBERWOLVES SIGN BRIAN BOWEN II, MATT LEWIS, ISAIAH MILLER AND CHRIS SILVA|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-sign-brian-bowen-ii-matt-lewis-isaiah-miller-and-chris-silva|website=NBA.com|date=September 20, 2021|access-date=September 20, 2021}}</ref> However, he was waived prior to the start of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Waive Brian Bowen II, Matt Lewis, Isaiah Miller And Chris Silva|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-waive-brian-bowen-ii-matt-lewis-isaiah-miller-and-chris-silva|website=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2021|access-date=October 17, 2021}}</ref> On October 26, he signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the [[Iowa Wolves]] as an affiliate player.<ref>{{cite web|title=Iowa Wolves Announce Training Camp Roster and Finalize Coaching Staff|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/iowa-wolves-announce-training-camp-roster-and-finalize-coaching-staff/n-5758384|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 26, 2021|access-date=November 2, 2021}}</ref>

===Salt Lake City Stars (2022–2024)===
In May 2022, Miller was invited to participate in a free agent camp by the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Joe|last=Coles|title=Utah Jazz, looking to find players that can contribute at the end of the roster, hold free agent camp|url=https://www.deseret.com/2022/5/31/23148413/utah-jazz-looking-to-find-players-that-contribute-at-the-end-of-the-roster-hold-nba-free-agent-camp|newspaper=Deseret News|date=May 31, 2022|access-date=May 31, 2022}}</ref> He subsequently made the Jazz [[2022 NBA Summer League|Summer League]] roster.<ref>{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz 2022 Salt Lake City Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/utah/team/1610612762/jazz|website=NBA.com|access-date=September 10, 2022}}</ref>

On August 3, 2022, Miller signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]],<ref>{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Trail Blazers Sign Isaiah Miller|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2022/08/trail-blazers-signing-isaiah-miller.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=August 3, 2022|access-date=August 4, 2022}}</ref> but was waived prior to the start of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title= Trail Blazers Waive Isaiah Miller and Jared Rhoden|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-waive-isaiah-miller-and-jared-rhoden|website=NBA.com|date=October 12, 2022|access-date=October 16, 2022}}</ref> On October 23, he joined the [[Salt Lake City Stars]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Stars Announce 2022-23 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/stars-announce-2022-23-training-camp-roster/n-5892964|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 23, 2022|access-date=October 23, 2022}}</ref>

On October 21, 2023, Miller signed with Utah, but was waived the same day<ref>{{cite web|first=Gabby|last=Hundman|title=Utah Jazz Sign and Waive Isaiah Miller|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-and-waive-isaiah-miller|website=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=November 4, 2023}}</ref> and on October 30, he rejoined the Stars.<ref>{{cite web|title=Stars Announce 2023-24 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/stars-announce-2023-24-training-camp-roster/n-6027250|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=November 4, 2023}}</ref>

===APR (2024)===
On July 31, 2024, Miller signed with [[APR BBC|APR]] of the [[Rwanda Basketball League]] and the [[Basketball Africa League]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=APR Basketball Club🏀🦁🇷🇼|title=NEW TRADE ALERT: Isaiah Miller, a point guard from Salt Lake City Stars of the NBA G League, has joined us. The 25-year-old American will be available for selection tonight as we face REG.|number=1818640066270335371|user=APRBBC_Official|date=July 31, 2024|access-date=July 31, 2024}}</ref> In August, APR won the inaugural [[Rwanda Basketball Cup]], behind Miller's 43-point performance in the final against [[REG BBC|REG]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Damas|last=Sikubwabo|title=APR wins inaugural Rwanda basketball cup tournament|url=https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/19086/sports/football/apr-wins-inaugural-rwanda-basketball-cup-tournament|work=The New Times|date=August 10, 2024|access-date=August 22, 2024}}</ref>

On September 23, 2024, Miller and APR won the RBL championship after they defeated [[Patriots BBC|Patriots]] in Game 6 of the finals. Miller was named the RBL playoffs MVP.<ref>{{cite web|first=Damas|last=Sikubwabo|title=PHOTOS: APR see off Patriots in Game 6, win record 15th championship|url=https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/20333/sports/basketball/photos-apr-see-off-patriots-in-game-6-win-record-15th-championship|work=The New Times|date=September 23, 2024|access-date=September 23, 2024}}</ref>

===Austin Spurs (2024–present)===
On October 13, 2024, Miller signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]], but was waived two days later.<ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Spurs Sign, Waive Isaiah Miller|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/spurs-sign-isaiah-miller.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 15, 2024|access-date=October 15, 2024}}</ref> On October 29, he joined the [[Austin Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Austin Spurs Announce 2024 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/austin-spurs-announce-2024-training-camp-roster/n-6160743|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 29, 2024|access-date=November 3, 2024}}</ref> On February 2, 2025, Miller had suffered a torn right [[anterior cruciate ligament]] and would miss the remainder of [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–25 season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Austin Spurs injury update - 02/05/25|url=https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-injury-update-02-05-25|date=February 6, 2025|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 6, 2025}}</ref>
